summary: Not as a read on direction. On 1h, long entries after the low dropped 2%, 3% or 5% under the open beat random, and so did entries after the high rose the same amount over it, at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles. Both sides beating random points to timing, not direction: these candles are volatile and the window rose, so price moved more after them. Below the 200-day SMA, the 5% drop did the same as random.

verdicts.text: Beat random on 1h at all three sizes, at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles, much like the drops. A move in either direction came before a bigger swing in a window that rose.
The 2% and 3% drops rest on one long SOL stretch, and without it they did the same as random. The 5% moves beat random only through SOL. On BTC and ETH they did the same as random.
Most daily settings had too few separate moves to judge. The high 5% over the open looked ahead, but it rests on one SOL stretch.

notes: On 1h, long entries after the low reached 2% under the open gave 7,853 entries in 1,611 separate moves. Twenty candles later they were 0.75% ahead of random entries, above a luck band of -0.16% to 0.34%. The result holds without its strongest stretch, between Dec 26, 2020 and Jan 23, 2021, and at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles. The high 2% over the open came out 0.8% ahead, so it made no difference which way the candle moved.

The gap grows with the size of the move. The low 3% under the open beat random by 1.4%, and the low 5% by 2.33%. The low 2% setting fires about two and a half times as often as the low 3%, and the low 3% about four times as often as the low 5%. Bigger candles come before bigger swings, and in a window that rose, that pushes these longs ahead of random entries.

Above the 200-day SMA, every 1h setting beat random: the low 2% by 0.75% and the low 5% by 2.44%. Below it, the low 5% under the open did the same as random, 0.01% after 20 candles. In downtrends, the low 2% and high 2% beat random at 20 candles only, so they are fragile there. The low 3% is the exception: it beat random in both regimes, by 0.84% in downtrends.

On 4h most of the 1h result falls apart. The low 2% beat random by 0.67%, but it rests on 1,912 SOL entries between Sep 1, 2020 and Sep 2, 2022. Without them it did the same as random. The high 5% beat random pooled, yet on BTC (-0.12%) and on ETH it did the same as random. Split by regime, it did the same as random in uptrends and in downtrends.

On daily candles, most settings had fewer than 30 separate moves, so they were never judged. The high 5% over the open ended 4.96% ahead of random, but 337 entries between Sep 3, 2020 and Sep 26, 2022 carry it. Without them it did the same as random. In downtrends it was 0.99% behind random, still inside the luck band.

Read a large 1h candle as a volatility marker, not as a direction. After a 3% or larger move from the open, price moved more over the next 20 candles than after a random candle, in a window that rose. That matters for how far your DCA steps and take profit sit inside the swing. Below the 200-day SMA, the low 5% setting added nothing, so pair it with a trend filter or leave it out. On 4h and daily, treat any gap as a SOL stretch, and test it on your own pair.
